Title: August 20, 2026 - Regular City Council Meeting
Overview: The Boulder City Council held its regular meeting with extended open comment on topics including Gaza divestment, a hunting ballot measure, wildfire-zone development, and Flock license plate readers, followed by a consent agenda approving a $400 million bond ballot item and other items. Council unanimously adopted ordinances 8771 and 8772 authorizing property acquisition for the North and South 30th Street safety projects. The board of the Downtown Commercial District then approved the sale of the Spruce Street parking lot at 2121 Broadway to a hotel developer by a 7-1 vote after a lengthy public hearing.

Topic1.Title: Open Public Comment
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke during open comment on Gaza and divestment, the Initiative 302 hunting amendment, a pause on high-density student housing in wildfire zones, and tax burdens. Council members and staff responded afterward, with staff noting a planned wildfire home-hardening presentation on August 27. Speakers were limited to two-minute time slots under the decorum rules read at the start.

Topic2.Title: Flock License Plate Reader Pause
Topic2.Summary: Staff confirmed a pause on the automated license plate reader RFP and said the city will not sign a contract until a more detailed community engagement plan is in place. The existing cameras remain in use on a month-to-month basis with the current provider. Staff also said additional guardrails are being considered and will be shared in an upcoming press release.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Bond Ordinance 8758
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3C and 3E through 3J unanimously after a resident objected to the roughly $400 million bond ordinance. Council members discussed the need for budget transparency, the possibility of an independent auditor, and whether the bond would affect the graduated income tax. Staff explained the Alpine Balsam housing funds and said no affordable housing fund money is going to the Western City campus.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up Check-In and Suspension of Rules
Topic4.Summary: Council did not call up item 4A, a landmark alteration certificate to relocate an accessory building at 1733 Canyon Boulevard. Council then voted unanimously to suspend procedural rules to allow three public hearings that evening.

Topic5.Title: North and South 30th Street Property Acquisition Ordinances
Topic5.Summary: Staff requested authority to acquire easements along North 30th and South 30th Street by negotiation or eminent domain to protect federal grant spending deadlines. The North 30th project costs about $9.3 million, with roughly half of about 50 properties needing temporary or permanent easements averaging under 1,000 square feet. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8771 for North 30th and Ordinance 8772 for South 30th, and staff said South 30th construction would finish a year ahead of North 30th.

Topic6.Title: Spruce Street Parking Lot Sale: Staff Presentation and Questions
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented an unsolicited offer from MALR Boulder LLC to buy the KGID-owned surface lot at 2121 Broadway for $5.8 million for a 110-room boutique hotel. The terms include six 30-year community benefit covenants covering affordable commercial space, public space, arts, contracting, energy performance, and alley access for First Congregational Church. A parking study found the 59 lost spaces could be absorbed by nearby garages, and council questioned water demand, Visit Boulder support, and the revenue impact on KGID.

Topic7.Title: Spruce Street Lot Public Hearing
Topic7.Summary: Nineteen speakers addressed the proposed sale, and most opposing speakers were from First Congregational Church, Trinity Lutheran, and local businesses. Their main concerns were loss of accessible parking for elderly and disabled visitors, congestion, and the lack of community process before the sale. Supporters, including the developer, cited the vibrancy of the Ramble Hotel in Denver, economic benefits, and the need for more downtown lodging for Sundance.

Topic8.Title: Council Deliberation and Board Vote on Spruce Lot Sale
Topic8.Summary: Council members said the sale would not approve the hotel design, since later site and concept review would still be required under normal development rules. Several members highlighted the long-term fiscal benefit of tax revenue from the hotel and the strength of the covenants, while others raised concerns about parking, water, and energy. The board then approved the purchase agreement by a 7-1 vote, with Council Member Adams voting no.
